headline: You are literally made of stardust—every atom in your body was forged in a star
universal_truth: We are not separate from the universe; we are the universe experiencing itself
fun_facts: Every element heavier than hydrogen and helium was created inside a star's nuclear furnace
The iron in your blood was forged in a supernova explosion billions of years ago
There are more stars in the universe than grains of sand on all of Earth's beaches
discussion_questions: How does knowing you're made of stardust change how you see yourself?
What do you think happens to stars—and to us—at the end?
If the universe is conscious through us, what's worth experiencing?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Tonight, when you look up at the stars, you're looking at your ancestors. Not metaphorically—literally. Every atom in your body except hydrogen was forged inside a dying star. You are stardust, looking back at the stars.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Stars are born, they live, and they die—sometimes violently. In their death throes, they scatter their insides across the cosmos. How does a ball of gas create the carbon in your cells, the oxygen you breathe?

options.text: Nuclear fusion smashes atoms together to build heavier ones
options.response: Exactly. Stars are element factories, fusing hydrogen into helium, then heavier and heavier elements.

options.text: Stars collect elements from space dust
options.response: Stars do gather material, but they also create new elements...

q1.title: Element Factories
q1.script: Stars spend most of their lives fusing hydrogen into helium. As they age, they fuse helium into carbon, carbon into oxygen, and so on up the periodic table. Our sun will make it to carbon. Bigger stars forge iron. Beyond iron? Only supernovas have enough energy.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Element Factories"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Supernova Gifts
q2.script: The iron in your blood, the calcium in your bones, the gold in any jewelry you wear—all of it was created in supernova explosions. When massive stars die, they explode with the energy of 100 billion suns, scattering their elemental creations across space.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Cosmic Abundance
q3.script: There are roughly 200 billion trillion stars in the observable universe—more than grains of sand on every beach on Earth. And around many of those stars, planets orbit. The universe is vast beyond comprehension, and we are its witnesses.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You're not in the universe—you ARE the universe. A part of it that became conscious, that can look back at the stars and wonder. The cosmos made you so it could understand itself.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 7—our first week together complete. Tomorrow, we'll explore something closer to home: what makes a real friend. Until then, remember: you're made of stars.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Cosmic Perspective - Zooming Out
growTrack.learning_objective: Practice seeing your life from a larger perspective
growTrack.activity: Tonight, spend 3 minutes looking at the stars (or if cloudy, imagine them). Consider that some of that light has traveled millions of years to reach you. Let that perspective inform one thing you're stressed about.
